summary: Richard Peace is among thousands of farmers who missed out as funding was snapped up in hours.

stories.title: Amber warning issued as Storm Austen threatens UK with strong winds and heavy rain
summary: The deep area of low pressure is expected to move close to the south of the UK early on Friday with south-west England set to bear the brunt.

stories.title: Massive wasps' nest in wildlife office dismantled
summary: The insects lived in a nature reserve office for four months.

stories.title: Estate records 'abundance' of wildlife despite drought
summary: Wimpole's "long-term approach to nature recovery" has seen more than 5,000 species recorded.

stories.title: Giant tunnel proposed to clean up Windermere's sewage problem
summary: The plan would eliminate sewage spills into Windermere, blamed for turning the water green.

stories.title: Huge fin whale filmed off Welsh coast
summary: Rhys Morgan captured footage of the world's second-largest whale species lunge feeding on his drone.

stories.title: Scientists finally uncover why statins can cause muscle pain
summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising reason why statins, the widely prescribed cholesterol-lowering drugs that help prevent heart attacks and strokes, can sometimes cause muscle pain, weakness, and even severe muscle damage.
Using advanced imaging technology, researchers discovered that statins can attach to a crucial protein in muscle cells and force open a channel that normally controls calcium flow.
This causes calcium to leak continuously, potentially damaging muscle tissue.

stories.title: Hurricane warning maps are improving, but a dangerous problem remains
summary: A new study reveals that improved hurricane forecast graphics may help people identify threatened areas without making them more likely to recognize the danger or take protective action.
Researchers also found that a widespread misunderstanding of the hurricane cone persists, highlighting a potentially dangerous gap between accurate forecasts and public preparedness.

stories.title: Astronomers uncover new secrets of the Universe’s first five minutes
summary: Scientists have achieved a major breakthrough in understanding the Universe’s earliest moments, measuring the amount of helium formed in the first five minutes after the Big Bang with unprecedented precision.
Using one of the world’s most powerful telescopes, an international team studied 15 remarkably pristine galaxies that act as cosmic time capsules, preserving clues from nearly 13.8 billion years ago.

stories.title: Scientists discover a bizarre Jurassic “squid” unlike anything ever seen
summary: Scientists have identified the “fattest” belemnite ever discovered, a bizarre, barrel-shaped squid relative that lived in Wyoming’s ancient seas 160 million years ago.
The exceptionally rare fossils reveal a creature unlike anything previously known, potentially a predator of smaller squid-like animals and a surprising survivor of a supposedly vanished family.

stories.title: Moment giant fin whale's huge mouth engulfs thousands of gallons of water
summary: Videographer Rhys Morgan captured footage of the worlds second largest whale lunge feeding on his drone.

stories.title: Your aging brain may be trading memory for something more valuable
summary: The aging brain may be undergoing a remarkable transformation rather than simply losing its abilities, shifting its focus from remembering details to understanding the bigger picture.
Scientists suggest this change could be an evolutionary adaptation that helps older adults develop wisdom and share decades of knowledge with younger generations.

stories.title: Scientists find a way to fight Alzheimer’s brain damage without removing toxic tau
summary: Scientists have found a promising way to protect the brain from Alzheimer’s-related damage by blocking immune cells that contribute to the destruction of neurons.
In mice, the treatment preserved roughly 40% more tissue in memory centers and improved memory, even without removing harmful tau protein buildup.

stories.title: Storm Austen to bring severe gales to UK as weather warning issued
summary: The first named storm of the season - Austen - will bring damaging winds and heavy rain to parts of the UK on Friday.

stories.title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies this week
summary: Clear skies permitting, skygazers could be able to spot as many as 10-20 meteors per hour as the shower peaks this week.

stories.title: NASA reveals 16 stunning galaxies hiding cosmic chaos
summary: NASA's stunning new gallery of 16 galaxies reveals colossal black hole jets, explosive star formation, and spectacular cosmic collisions through the combined power of Chandra, James Webb, Hubble, and other telescopes.
These extraordinary images expose the hidden forces shaping galaxies across the universe and offer clues about the Milky Way's own past and future.

stories.title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving
summary: Conservationists say that, with red squirrels dwindling in the UK, Jersey is an "important refuge".

stories.title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change
summary: The new chair of the Climate Change Committee is spending two days in Northern Ireland on a fact-finding mission.

stories.title: Scientists discover a surprising link between vitamin C and cancer survival
summary: A surprising clinical trial suggests that taking vitamin C daily could improve survival in people with precancerous blood disorders and early-stage blood cancers.
Patients receiving the supplement had fewer adverse events and showed a promising survival advantage, raising hopes that a common vitamin could help protect against leukemia-related complications.

stories.title: Scientists reach the ultimate quantum limit on a surface
summary: Scientists have achieved a quantum breakthrough by creating an ultra-clean surface where individual molecules can maintain their delicate quantum properties at the fundamental limit.
The discovery could unlock unprecedented control over molecules and help drive the next generation of quantum technologies.

stories.title: NASA solves a strange mystery hidden inside asteroid Bennu’s boulders
summary: NASA scientists have finally uncovered why asteroid Bennu loses heat so quickly despite being covered in massive boulders.
Samples returned to Earth reveal that its rocks are filled with hidden cracks, solving a mystery that has puzzled researchers for years.

stories.title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world
summary: As the strongest El Niño on record continues to intensify, what impacts on weather patterns are already being felt across the globe?
Sarah Keith-Lucas looks at the evidence.
